svg.title: SPECTRA block diagram · Part 2 of 3 — core 0 pipeline (core 1 is an identical instance)
svg.text: SPECTRA block diagram · Part 2 of 3 — core 0 pipeline (core 1 is an identical instance)
3 stages: IF/ID · EX · MEM/WB; pipeline registers: fetch PC, ID/EX, EX/MEM-WB. Dashed amber boxes link to Part 1 (system) and Part 3 (data side).
a write is read back in
decides when stages wait or are cleared:
waits for memory and MUL / DIV, clears
SW0 on: forwards · SW0 off: 1-cycle wait

g.text: 1 / 6 · Fetch The fetch PC addresses I-cache 0; a hit answers the next cycle, a miss refills a line through core 0's mem delay
2 / 6 · Decode ID decodes, reads two registers and the immediate; the hazard unit checks the dependence on the instruction in EX
3 / 6 · Execute EX: forwarding muxes pick the operands, the ALU or MUL / DIV computes; a busy MUL / DIV holds the pipeline
4 / 6 · Taken branch Branches, JAL and JALR resolve in EX: the PC jumps to the target and the two younger instructions are squashed
5 / 6 · Load / store MEM/WB sends one request on D-port 0 to the arbiter; every stage freezes until ready (a D-cache hit: 2 cycles)
6 / 6 · Write-back The result is written to the register file and forwarded to EX; every retired instruction is counted

svg.text: • Taken branch / JAL / JALR: resolved in EX, the 2 younger instructions are squashed (2 cycles); no predictor. FWD = 0: a dependence at distance 1 waits 1 cycle.
• An illegal instruction (FENCE, ECALL, CSR …) decodes as a no-op: it writes and stores nothing. The firmware uses RV32I + M only.
